business_model.claim: For employer services, prices are negotiated at market rates. They are paid by employers or by third-party administrators.

business_model.claim: Workers' compensation revenue is driven by visit volume and rate growth. Rate-driven growth in visit-related revenue averaged approximately 3% a year from 2016 to 2025.

business_model.claim: Management tracks two key operating metrics for the centers: visits per day (VPD) and revenue per visit. VPD is total visits divided by business days.

business_model.claim: Rate increases in 2025 came from state fee schedule increases for workers' compensation and from higher employer services rates.

business_model.basis: stated in P6 facility count table

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal: demand is higher in summer. Revenue also varies with the number of business days in each quarter.

business_model.claim: Cost of services is the largest expense. It was 426,650 against revenue of 622,122 in Q3 2026 (table in thousands).

growth_thesis.claim: Q3 2026 revenue was 622,122 versus 572,800 a year earlier (table in thousands), a reported increase of 8.6%.
quotes: Revenue of $622.1 million, an increase of 8.6% from $572.8 million in Q3 2025

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 1, patient visit volume: Q3 2026 visits were 3,731,956, or 58,312 visits per day, up 4.9% from 55,589.
quotes: Patient visits of 3,731,956, or 58,312 visits per day, an increase of 4.9% from 55,589 visits per day in Q3 2025

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Driver 1: work-related injuries must not decline. The company lists falling injury frequency as a risk to its business.
quotes: A decline in workplace injuries and illness may cause the number of workers’ compensation claims to decrease, which may adversely affect our business.

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Driver 1: US employment must keep supporting demand. The 10-K cites 159.4 million non-farm employees at end of 2025.
quotes: The United States workforce is large and growing with 159.4 million non-farm employees as of the end of 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, with an overall increase of 6% compared to 2019 levels.

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 2, revenue per visit: Q3 2026 revenue per visit was $152.14, up 3.3% from $147.31. Workers' compensation revenue per visit was $219.24 versus $211.82.
quotes: Revenue per visit of $152.14, an increase of 3.3% from $147.31 in Q3 2025

growth_thesis.claim: The company attributes revenue growth to both visit volume and rate growth, with 2025 rate gains coming from state fee schedules and employer services pricing.
quotes: Our workers’ compensation revenue is driven by a combination of visit volume and rate growth.

We experienced a higher revenue per visit principally due to increases in the reimbursement rates payable pursuant to certain state fee schedules for workers’ compensation visits, as well as increases in our employer services rates, during the year ended December 31, 2025.

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Driver 2: states must keep raising fee schedule rates at least as fast as cost inflation. The company does not control these rates.
quotes: Given that we do not control these processes, we may be subject to financial risks, including decreased revenue and profitability, if individual jurisdictions reduce rates or do not routinely raise rates of reimbursement in a manner that keeps pace with the inflation of our costs of service.

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 3, acquisitions: 2025 revenue growth of 13.9% included 72 acquired occupational health centers and over 240 acquired onsite locations.
quotes: Revenue increased 13.9% to $2,163.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $1,900.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, driven by organic increases in both volume of patient visits and revenue per visit and due to the addition of 72 occupational health centers that were acquired through acquisitions in March 2025 and over 240 onsite locations that were acquired through acquisition in June 2025.

growth_thesis.claim: Acquisition activity was smaller in 2026: 7 centers acquired in nine months, against 72 a year earlier. Cash for business combinations was (9,995) versus (333,300) (table in thousands).
quotes: M&A pipeline remains strong, evaluating bolt-on acquisitions of both occupational health centers and onsite health clinics

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Driver 3: acquisitions must succeed and avoid unforeseen liabilities, which the company lists as a risk.
quotes: Current and future acquisitions may use significant resources, may be unsuccessful, and could expose us to unforeseen liabilities.

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 4, new centers: occupational health centers rose from 628 to 639 in nine months of 2026. This included 5 de novos and 7 acquisitions, net of 1 closure.
quotes: Number of occupational health centers—end of period | 639 | 628

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 5, onsite health clinics: clinic count was 423 versus 413. The segment's share of nine-month revenue was 6% versus 5%.
quotes: Number of onsite health clinics—end of period | 423 | 413

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Drivers 1 and 5: the company must keep its significant employer customer, payor and network relationships.
quotes: The loss of our significant employer customers, payor or network relationships could cause a material decline in our profitability and operating performance.

growth_thesis.claim: Driver 6, operating leverage: Q3 2026 income from operations rose 21.9% to 115,199 from 94,472 (table in thousands). Cost of services rose only 5.2%.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA Margin increased to 22.5%, an expansion of 178 basis points year over year

growth_thesis.claim: Condition for Driver 6: labor costs must stay contained. The company says it has already seen lower profitability from rising labor costs.
quotes: We have experienced and may continue to experience decreased profitability due to increased labor costs.
The percentage of revenue decreased primarily due to increased staffing efficiencies, relative to a 13.9% increase in revenue during the period.
